title: Whiteboard W4: the 3-line Consequence Gate claim-lookup patch and the SR002 / integrity pin
problem: Step 11 of policy/consequence_gate.py checks that a proposal or grant was not dispatched before by copying every grant_dispatch record. One claim is written per Gate-mediated act, so the check grows with history. On #196 only the newest 1024 payloads stay in memory, so each older claim is read back from the ledger file on every act. The 3-line fix (select by proposal_id, then by grant_id) changes the Gate's bytes, which are pinned by the live integrity check (governance/integrity/manifest.json, founder-signed authorizations only), the SR-001/SR-002 subject bindings (evolution/repair/subjects.py) and many frozen evaluations.
founder_intent_refs: Whiteboard 2026-11-13 (issue #96 comment 6852550499), item W4; founder approval of the authority note, comment 6852618695
docs/collaboration/FINDING-LEDGER-APPEND-COST-2026-10-14.md (#137) section 'Founder decision: the Gate's claim scan'
governance/integrity/README.md: only a signature by an enrolled founder key authorizes a protected artifact
baseline: #196 f383fd26: the Gate scans every grant_dispatch record on every act; policy/consequence_gate.py at sha256 1c189be5...

alternatives.name: Apply the 3-line patch now
alternatives.description: Replace the scan with two select() lookups and re-bind the pins.
advantages: Gate act cost flat in history (0.00 ms at 6,000 claims vs 33.95 ms)
disadvantages: Fails the live integrity check (CI job 3) until an enrolled founder key signs the new digest; no key is enrolled
alternatives.revival_evidence: Alfonso enrolls his key and signs INTEGRITY_AUTHORIZE for the patched digest

alternatives.name: Keep claim payloads resident (ledger-only)
alternatives.description: Exempt grant_dispatch payloads from RESIDENT_RECORDS eviction so the scan never reads the file.
disadvantages: Spends memory W5 is trying to bound
alternatives.revival_evidence: The Gate stays frozen for a long time and the per-act cost becomes the measured bottleneck

alternatives.name: Re-bind SR002 by editing subjects.py
alternatives.description: Update the SR002 tuple to the new digest.
disadvantages: SR002 is a fixed source binding for past evaluations; rewriting it falsifies what those evaluations attest. A new binding (SR-003) is the honest route

alternatives.name: Land only the equivalence guard test now
alternatives.description: Pin step 11's refusal by proposal and by grant separately, with no Gate change.
advantages: Green today; proves the patch refuses exactly what the scan refuses before the founder signs

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Per-act cost grows about 5.7 us per prior claim: about 0.4 s per act after 50 days of one minute-cadence mission (72,000 claims) and about 3 s after a year. It runs under the Body's turn lock, so it delays every mission.

roles.position: The Gate is a founder-ratified artifact; agents must not move its digest.
material_concerns: Whiteboard authority note: agents decide reversible work; Gate and Constitution need a founder signature (AGENTS.md)

roles.position: The patch is semantically the same check: select() re-checks every answer against the record, and the ledger lock is an RLock, so calling it under the Gate's held lock is safe.
material_concerns: The scan raises KeyError on a malformed claim; select() treats it as not matching. Only the Gate writes claims, with both fields.

roles.position: A future edit could keep only one of the two lookups and still pass the existing suite: no test refused by grant alone.
material_concerns: Add a test per field; check it kills the one-field mutant

roles.position: The cost is real and linear; measured, not estimated.
material_concerns: Microbenchmark on #196 f383fd26 (provenance.ledger.EvidenceLedger, file-backed, default RESIDENT_RECORDS=1024, 13 records per Gate act, median of 7): Gate's by_type scan 3.03 / 13.86 / 33.95 ms at 600 / 2,400 / 6,000 prior claims; the 3-line select patch 0.00 ms at each size. With every payload resident: 1.03 / 5.40 / 11.97 ms.

roles.position: Frozen evaluations record the old digest as their input; they stay true. Re-binding SR002 in place would not.
material_concerns: A changed Gate needs new evaluation bindings (SR-003), not edits to SR002 or freeze files
evidence_refs: AGENTS.md: new runs get new paths
